title: Data Handling: Pictographs, Bar Graphs and Tallies
seo_title: Grade 3 Data Handling Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_code: Grade 3: Collect, sort, represent and interpret data
standard_text: Collect and sort objects; collect data; represent data in pictographs and bar graphs; analyse and interpret data and report on it.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: pictographs with a key, bar graphs, tally tables and data stories. 100 questions with pictures and memos.
key_sub: Read across from the top of the bar.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the title and the key first.
  • In a pictograph, one picture may stand for 2, 5 or 10.
  • In a bar graph, read across from the top of the bar to the scale.
  • Compare by subtracting: how many more?

Examples

Example

Key: 1 picture = 5; 3 pictures

3 × 5

Answer: 15

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The keyMultiply by the key.
Between marksFind the middle value.
Most or fewestFewest is the smallest.

faq.a: Grade R to Grade 3 in South African schools. Grade 3 is the last year; learners are about 8 to 9 years old.
It tells what each picture is worth.
To answer a question and make a decision.

items.q: How many votes did Green get?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 votes. The Green row has 5 circles: 5 × 2 = 10 votes.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 learners. The Bike row has 3 stars: 3 × 5 = 15 learners.

items.q: How many points did Hawk House get?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 10 points. The Hawk row has 1 square and half a square: 1 × 10 = 10, and half of 10 is 5, so 10 + 5 = 15 points.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 books. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 books, not 1.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 stickers. The Lwazi row has 3 stars: 3 × 5 = 15 stickers.

items.q: Which row shows the most books?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the most squares shows the most. The Ofentse row has 6 squares: 6 × 2 = 12 books.

items.q: Each star stands for 2 books. Ofentse read 9 books. How many stars should be in her row?
items.e: Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8. 4 whole stars make 8. 1 more is half of 2, so add half a star. Draw 4 and a half stars.
Look at the key: each star stands for 2 birds. The Robin row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 birds.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a square stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole square = 10 cakes. Half a square is half of 10, which is 5 cakes, not 1.

items.q: Which row shows 7 learners?
items.e: Half a circle is 1, so 7 learners is 3 and a half circles. The Rabbit row has 3 circles and half a circle: 3 × 2 = 6, and half of 2 is 1, so 6 + 1 = 7 learners.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 learners. The Rugby row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 10 = 30, and half of 10 is 5, so 30 + 5 = 35 learners.

items.q: Which row shows the fewest shells?
items.e: Every square stands for the same number, so the row with the fewest squares shows the fewest. The Dumisani row has 1 square: 1 × 5 = 5 shells.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 learners. 45 learners walk to school. How many circles should be in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40. 4 whole circles make 40. 5 more is half of 10, so add half a circle. Draw 4 and a half circles.
Look at the key: each star stands for 5 votes. The Orange row has 4 stars: 4 × 5 = 20 votes.

items.q: How many worms were found?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 2 minibeasts. The Worm row has 2 squares and half a square: 2 × 2 = 4, and half of 2 is 1, so 4 + 1 = 5 minibeasts.

items.q: In this pictogram, what does half a circle stand for?
items.e: The key says one whole circle = 10 cans. Half a circle is half of 10, which is 5 cans, not 1.

items.q: How many worms were found?
items.e: Look at the key: each square stands for 5 minibeasts. The Worm row has 3 squares: 3 × 5 = 15 minibeasts.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 votes. Red got 30 votes. How many squares should be in the Red row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 30: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 squares. Check: 6 × 5 = 30.
Look at the key: each star stands for 10 cans. The 3B row has 3 stars and half a star: 3 × 10 = 30, and half of 10 is 5, so 30 + 5 = 35 cans.

items.q: How many stickers has Lwazi got?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle stands for 2 stickers. The Lwazi row has 5 circles: 5 × 2 = 10 stickers.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many votes did Orange get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Orange bar ends on the line for 10. So the answer is 10 votes.

items.q: How many points did Owl House get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Owl bar ends on the line for 20. So the answer is 20 points.

items.q: How many learners come by bus to school?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Bus bar ends halfway between 30 and 40, so it shows 35. So the answer is 35 learners.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Blue tit bar ends on the line for 2. So the answer is 2 birds.

items.q: Which bar shows 25 cans?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Find 25 on the scale. The 3B bar ends on the line for 25.

items.q: How many space books were borrowed?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Space bar ends halfway between 10 and 20, so it shows 15. So the answer is 15 books.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Each line is 5 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 5s.

items.q: Which bar shows the most stickers?
items.e: The Ethan bar is the tallest one. The Ethan bar ends on the line for 14. It shows 14 stickers.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Tuesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. The Tue bar ends halfway between 40 and 50, so it shows 45. So the answer is 45 cakes.

items.q: How many books did Ruan read?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Ruan bar ends on the line for 35. So the answer is 35 books.

items.q: How many votes did Green get?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Green bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 votes.

items.q: How many spiders were found?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. The Spider bar ends on the line for 30. So the answer is 30 minibeasts.

items.q: How many shells did Lerato find?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Lerato bar ends halfway between 2 and 4, so it shows 3. So the answer is 3 shells.

items.q: Which bar shows 15 books?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Find 15 on the scale. The Animals bar ends halfway between 10 and 20, so it shows 15.

items.q: Which bar shows the most shells?
items.e: The Dumisani bar is the tallest one. The Dumisani bar ends on the line for 35. It shows 35 shells.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Wednesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Wed bar ends halfway between 8 and 10, so it shows 9. So the answer is 9 cakes.

items.q: Which bar shows 2 learners?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Find 2 on the scale. The Netball bar ends on the line for 2.

items.q: What does the scale on this bar chart go up in?
items.e: Read the numbers on the scale: 0, 2, 4, 6 … Each line is 2 more than the one before, so the scale goes up in 2s.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Tuesday?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. The Tue bar ends on the line for 6. So the answer is 6 cakes.

items.q: How many snails were found?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Snail row has 1 group of 5 and 4 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: How many worms were found?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Worm row has 3 groups of 5 and 3 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 3 = 18.

items.q: How many learners chose soccer?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Soccer row has 1 group of 5 and 1 more: 1 × 5 = 5, and 5 + 1 = 6.

items.q: Which row shows 18 learners?
items.e: 18 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 3. Look for 3 groups of 5 and 3 single marks. That is the Cricket row.

items.q: How many votes did Apple get?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Apple row has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more: 2 × 5 = 10, and 10 + 2 = 12.

items.q: How many votes are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Apple 12, Banana 11, Grapes 14, Pear 10. Then add: 12 + 11 + 14 + 10 = 47 votes.

items.q: How many vans went past the school?
items.e: Each group of 5 is four lines with one line across. The Van row has 3 groups of 5 and 2 more: 3 × 5 = 15, and 15 + 2 = 17.

items.q: What is the difference between the biggest and the smallest number of vehicles?
items.e: The biggest is Van (17). The smallest is Bus (12). Difference means subtract: 17 − 12 = 5.

items.q: Which row shows 18 cars?
items.e: 18 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 3. Look for 3 groups of 5 and 3 single marks. That is the Black row.

items.q: How many cars are shown in the tally chart altogether?
items.e: Count each row: Black 18, White 8, Silver 9, Red 4. Then add: 18 + 8 + 9 + 4 = 39 cars.

items.q: How many worms did class 3A find?
items.e: Find the Worms row, then go across to the Class 3A column. The cell says 5.

items.q: How many snails did the two classes find altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Snails row: 10 + 13 = 23.

items.q: How many more spiders did class 3B find than class 3A?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 18 − 3 = 15.

items.q: Which minibeast did the two classes find the most of altogether?
items.e: Add each row: Ladybirds 7 + 12 = 19, Worms 5 + 11 = 16, Snails 10 + 13 = 23, Spiders 3 + 18 = 21. The biggest total is 23, for snails.

items.q: How many books did Kabelo read in week 2?
items.e: Find the Kabelo row, then go across to the Week 2 column. The cell says 10.

items.q: How many books did the four learners read in week 2?
items.e: Add the whole Week 2 column: 10 + 4 + 2 + 11 = 27.

items.q: How many more books did Zanele read in week 1 than in week 2?
items.e: How many more means find the difference: 12 − 4 = 8.

items.q: How many learners had a hot dinner on Monday?
items.e: Find the Monday row, then go across to the Hot dinner column. The cell says 12.

items.q: How many learners had lunch on Tuesday altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Add the two cells in the Tuesday row: 15 + 20 = 35.

items.q: How many learners had a hot dinner from Monday to Thursday?
items.e: Add the whole Hot dinner column: 12 + 15 + 22 + 10 = 59.

items.q: How many more stickers has Precious got than Ethan?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Precious 7 and Ethan 2. How many more means find the difference: 7 − 2 = 5 stickers.
Each star = 5. Purple 2 × 5 = 10 and Green 5 × 5 = 25. Altogether means add: 10 + 25 = 35 votes.

items.q: How many more worms were found than spiders?
items.e: Each circle = 2, so half a circle = 1. Worm 4 × 2 + 1 = 9 and Spider 2 × 2 + 1 = 5. How many more means find the difference: 9 − 5 = 4 minibeasts.

items.q: How many cakes were sold on Tuesday and Wednesday altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Tue 10 and Wed 15. Altogether means add: 10 + 15 = 25 cakes.

items.q: How many shells did they find altogether?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Read every bar: Lerato 4, Dumisani 2, Lungile 6, Ethan 7. Add them: 4 + 2 + 6 + 7 = 19 shells.

items.q: How many more learners walk to school than cycle?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Walk 20 and Bike 15. How many more means find the difference: 20 − 15 = 5 learners.

items.q: How many points did Falcon and Hawk get altogether?
items.e: Each square = 10, so half a square = 5. Falcon 5 × 10 = 50 and Hawk 1 × 10 = 10. Altogether means add: 50 + 10 = 60 points.

items.q: How many fewer books did Ruan read than Zinhle?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Zinhle 12 and Ruan 6. How many fewer means find the difference: 12 − 6 = 6 books.

items.q: How many more blue tits were seen than sparrows and robins together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 5s. Blue tit 20, Sparrow 5 and Robin 10. Step 1: sparrows and robins together: 5 + 10 = 15. Step 2: 20 − 15 = 5 birds.

items.q: How many books were borrowed altogether?
items.e: Each square = 5. Read every row: Sport 4 × 5 = 20, Mystery 1 × 5 = 5, Animals 2 × 5 = 10, Space 3 × 5 = 15. Add them: 20 + 5 + 10 + 15 = 50 books.

items.q: How many more votes did Pear get than Banana?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Pear 4 × 10 + 5 = 45 and Banana 3 × 10 + 5 = 35. How many more means find the difference: 45 − 35 = 10 votes.
Each star = 2, so half a star = 1. Green 5 × 2 + 1 = 11, Yellow 3 × 2 + 1 = 7 and Red 4 × 2 + 1 = 9. Step 1: Yellow and Red together: 7 + 9 = 16. Step 2: 16 − 11 = 5 votes fewer.

items.q: Grade 3 want to collect 200 cans altogether. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. Step 1: read every bar and add: 60 + 40 + 50 + 30 = 180. Step 2: 200 − 180 = 20 cans.

items.q: How many more votes did Banana get than Apple and Pear together?
items.e: Each circle = 10, so half a circle = 5. Banana 6 × 10 = 60, Apple 1 × 10 = 10 and Pear 1 × 10 + 5 = 15. Step 1: Apple and Pear together: 10 + 15 = 25. Step 2: 60 − 25 = 35 votes.
Each star = 5. Scooter 3 × 5 = 15 and Bus 1 × 5 = 5. How many fewer means find the difference: 15 − 5 = 10 learners.

items.q: How many fewer cans did class 3D collect than 3C and 3B together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 10s. 3D 40, 3C 20 and 3B 30. Step 1: 3C and 3B together: 20 + 30 = 50. Step 2: 50 − 40 = 10 cans fewer.

items.q: The learners want to read 100 books altogether this term. How many more books must they read?
items.e: Each circle = 5. Step 1: read every row and add: 5 + 10 + 25 + 20 = 60. Step 2: 100 − 60 = 40 books.

items.q: How many more spiders were found than woodlice and snails together?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Spider 11, Woodlouse 2 and Snail 5. Step 1: woodlice and snails together: 2 + 5 = 7. Step 2: 11 − 7 = 4 minibeasts.

items.q: How many more votes did Orange get than Grapes?
items.e: The scale goes up in 2s. Orange 6 and Grapes 4. How many more means find the difference: 6 − 4 = 2 votes.
Each star = 5. Dumisani 1 × 5 = 5 and Lerato 6 × 5 = 30. Altogether means add: 5 + 30 = 35 shells.

items.q: Favourite fruit: Apple 8, Pear 5, Plum 10, Kiwi 3. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one bar is one line too high.

items.q: Minibeasts found: Ant 15, Worm 25, Snail 10, Slug 35. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (the scale goes up in 5s). B: two bars are the wrong way round; C: one bar is one line too high; D: one bar is one line too low.

items.q: Favourite colour: Red 40, Blue 25, Pink 60, Green 30. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: D matches every number (the scale goes up in 10s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); C: one bar is one line too high.
B matches every number (each symbol = 2). A: two rows are the wrong way round; C: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Cakes sold: Mon 20, Tue 35, Wed 15, Thu 40. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (each symbol = 10). A: two rows are the wrong way round; B: a half symbol is drawn as a whole symbol; D: one row has a symbol too many.

items.q: Pets: Dog 15, Cat 10, Fish 20, Bird 5. Which pictogram shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (each symbol = 5). B: two rows are the wrong way round; C: one row has a symbol too many; D: one row is missing a symbol.

items.q: Grade 3 voted for their favourite fruit. How many more learners chose grapes than pears?
items.e: Each circle = 2 votes, so half a circle = 1. Grapes: 5 × 2 = 10. Pear: 1 × 2 + 1 = 3. How many more means subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. (Half a circle is 1 here, because half of 2 is 1.)

items.q: How many more woodlice than snails did the class find?
items.e: Woodlice: 16. Snails: 6. How many more means subtract: 16 − 6 = 10. (5 is the number of grid spaces between the bars, not the number of minibeasts.)
Each star = 5 books. Ruan has 5 stars: 5 × 5 = 25 books. 40 − 25 = 15 more books. (35 comes from counting the stars as 5 books.)
Zinhle: 3 stars, 3 × 5 = 15. Thandi: 2 stars, 2 × 5 = 10. Altogether: 15 + 10 = 25 books. (5 is the difference, or the number of stars.)

items.q: Art club has space for 15 children. How many more children can join Art club?
items.e: Art: 1 group of 5 and 3 more = 8. 15 − 8 = 7 more children. (Counting the group of 5 as 4 gives 7 children in Art, and a wrong answer of 8.)

items.q: How many more children go to Soccer club than to Choir and Chess together?
items.e: Soccer: 3 groups of 5 and 1 more = 16. Step 1: Choir and Chess together: 7 + 5 = 12. Step 2: 16 − 12 = 4.

items.q: How many fewer points has Hawk House got than Falcon House?
items.e: Falcon: 50. Hawk: halfway between 20 and 30, so 25. 50 − 25 = 25 points. (Reading Hawk as 20 gives 30.)

items.q: There are 28 learners in the class. Each learner chose one sport. The bar for cricket is missing. How many learners chose cricket?
items.e: Step 1: add the other bars: 10 + 7 + 6 = 23. Step 2: 28 − 23 = 5 learners chose cricket. (Netball ends halfway between 6 and 8, so it is 7, not 6.)

items.q: How many snails did the two classes find altogether?
items.e: Find the Snails row: 7 and 15. Altogether means add: 7 + 15 = 22. (19 is 12 + 7, which adds down the Class 3A column instead.)

items.q: Each learner has one pet. How many learners are shown altogether?
items.e: Each square = 2 learners, so half a square = 1. Dog 9, cat 6, fish 3, rabbit 4. 9 + 6 + 3 + 4 = 22. (Counting the squares gives 11. Leaving out the half squares gives 20.)

items.q: Sibusiso wants to draw a pictogram of 40, 30, 50 and 20 votes. Which key needs the fewest symbols?
items.e: The bigger the key, the fewer symbols you draw. With 1 symbol = 10 votes, 40 votes is just 4 symbols. With 1 symbol = 2 votes it would be 20 symbols.

items.q: How many fewer chocolate ice creams were sold than vanilla and mint ice creams together?
items.e: Step 1: vanilla and mint together: 35 + 15 = 50. Step 2: chocolate is 45. 50 − 45 = 5 fewer.

items.q: Favourite fruit: Apple 8, Pear 5, Plum 10, Kiwi 3. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: C matches every number (the scale goes up in 2s). A: two bars are the wrong way round; B: a bar is on the line below (it should be halfway between two lines); D: one bar is one line too high.

items.q: Minibeasts found: Ant 15, Worm 25, Snail 10, Slug 35. Which bar chart shows these numbers?
items.e: A matches every number (the scale goes up in 5s). B: two bars are the wrong way round; C: one bar is one line too high; D: one bar is one line too low.
